A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EKAN research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite retitling and reformatting.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original EKAN experiments on particle scattering, the three-body problem, and top quark tagging, although some baseline results are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: Section 6 retains the original experiments, and Appendix C additionally reports EKAN inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The gated basis functions, equivariant linear weights, grid updates, lift layer, and stacked architecture remain unchanged. Added motivation and notation clarifications do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same particle-scattering, planar three-body prediction, and top-quark classification tasks. Top-quark inputs remain the three constituents with highest transverse momentum; timing measurements use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same MLP, KAN, and group-specific EMLP comparators. The specialized top-quark methods newly cited in Section 6.3 are discussed but not evaluated in Table 3.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds inference latency in milliseconds per data point as an evaluation metric, including measurements across five existing parameter budgets. Previously reported data splits, model configurations, training budgets, and predictive metrics remain unchanged; detailed timing procedures are not supplied.

E4.justification: New Table 5 examines how EKAN inference latency varies with parameter count on the three-body task. This adds a limited computational-efficiency analysis beyond the retained prediction-error comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs with different random seeds and mean ± standard deviation for Tables 1–3. The new timing results introduce no repetition counts, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All predictive means and standard deviations in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. Appendix C newly reports approximately 18 ms per particle-scattering example, 13 ms per top-quark example, and 7, 12, 13, 14, and 16 ms across the five three-body parameter budgets in Table 5.

T1.justification: The mathematical constructions, Theorem 1, its Appendix B proof, and Appendix A generators retain the same substance. Explicit integer domains and small symbol corrections clarify existing notation without changing assumptions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty, equivariance, predictive-performance, and parameter-efficiency claims, including comparable top-quark performance using 26% of EMLP's parameters.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly motivates gating through the difficulty of directly imposing equivariance on nonlinear spline functions. Section 6.3 explains the existing focus on general architectures and identifies integration with task-specific models as future work.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds inference-time information alongside the retained RTX 3090 hardware and training details. Conversely, v2 removes the direct Zenodo DOI link for the top-quark dataset while retaining its bibliographic citation.

R1.justification: v2 adds ten references covering equivariant graph networks, equivariant self-supervised learning, and specialized jet-tagging methods. These modestly broaden the context and clarify comparator positioning while retaining the central relationship to EMLP and KAN.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, numbers background and related-work subsections, and makes localized explanatory and notation edits. Specific appendix references become generic Supplementary Material references, but most prose and the main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: The document switches throughout from one column to two columns. Figures 1–3 are reused but enlarged and repositioned; Tables 1–4 shrink substantially into single columns with captions below, and Table 5 is added. The appendices receive a separate Supplementary Material heading and layout.

improvement.justification: New timing evidence and clearer gating motivation and comparator scope improve the paper's technical context. However, Tables 1–4 shrink from roughly 6–8-point to 3.6–4.5-point text, reducing readability, and the direct dataset link disappears. With the main results and theory unchanged, these limited informational gains and concrete presentation/access losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
